newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks open lower, budget disappoints.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks open lower, budget disappoints.

text.p: The Australian share market headed lower at the open on Wednesday after U.S. markets came off the boil and Tuesday's federal budget failed to excite investors.
The All Ordinaries index lost 13.9 points to 2,520.4.

Brokers said the 1997/98 federal budget had not provided anything to encourage investors to extend the market's recent strong run with falls in bond, futures and currency markets signalling a weaker tone from the start.

"It is a budget that relies on economic growth and nothing more," said Stuart Smith, senior dealer at Lance Jones, adding that combined with a interest rate concerns in the U.S., many investors were still reluctant to commit funds.
"Until confidence comes back you won't see the mature conservative investor come into our market, and I don't know that this budget is enough to twist their arms."

Media giant News Corp was hardest hit among the leaders, losing 2.5 percent to A$5.78 (US$4.48) as traders showed concern over its Echostar situation and displeasure at talk of plans to buy the Dodgers baseball franchise for more than US$350 million.
Miner CRA held up best among the leaders, holding steady at A$19.80 after its dual listed sibling RTZ Plc hit a 12 month high in London trading.
Major gold miner Newcrest Mining Ltd bucked the trend, jumping nine percent to an intraday high of A$3.50 after it said managing director John Quinn had resigned.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about seven to five, while about 44 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
